headline: 3-0 vs. 3-0, and the Miami clock is the scouting report
dek: Patrick Mahomes went 20-of-24 for 246 yards and two touchdowns in a 24-10 win at Hard Rock Stadium; the 88 rushing yards, 3-of-7 on third down, and 25:39 of possession now meet the 3-0 Raiders on Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT.
videoHook: You scored 24 in Miami and still lost the football. Allegiant is 3-0, Maxx Crosby is the next snap, and Week 4 is where this start either becomes the West or just a sample.
theEdge: ESPN FPI at 69.6 percent and DraftKings hanging Chiefs -4.5 on a 47.5 total make Kansas City a road favorite against another unbeaten AFC West club; Polymarket’s 8.6 percent Super Bowl price is how the market treats a 3-0 team that just won 24-10 with 18 first downs and 25:39 of possession.

storyline.lede: Kansas City is 3-0 because Patrick Mahomes still ends drives, not because the Chiefs won the game of football in Miami. A 24-10 result at Hard Rock Stadium was built on a 20-of-24, 246-yard afternoon, a 10-yard Kenneth Walker touchdown 2:06 into the game, and two takeaways — L. Sneed forcing and recovering a Malik Willis fumble, George Karlaftis intercepting Willis — while the Dolphins posted 19 first downs, went 8-of-16 on third down, rushed for 119 yards, and held the ball 34:21. That is the tape that actually travels to Allegiant Stadium, where another 3-0 AFC West locker room is waiting and early control of the division is on the table.
body: The live identity is still Mahomes plus Walker, not a complete offense. Walker carried 18 times for 70 yards and the opening touchdown and finished with 20 touches; Rashee Rice caught 7 balls for 88 yards; the team ran 25 times for 88 yards and converted 3-of-7 on third down. Miami’s 31 rushes and 34:21 of possession did not beat Kansas City on the scoreboard, but they did describe a defense that tackled and a staff that won with explosives and takeaways more than with downs. Steve Spagnuolo’s group recorded 0 sacks and 1 QB hit. Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy got a clean enough pocket — 0 sacks, 5 QB hits on Mahomes — and still lost the clock.

Week 4 is not a coronation lap. The Raiders are 3-0, Kirk Cousins has been better than the preseason discount, Tyler Linderbaum has the interior looking grown, and Maxx Crosby does not need Kansas City’s 20-of-24 clip to know where to rush. Arrowhead Addict is right that something has to give when two unbeaten West clubs meet, and right again that Las Vegas has more riding on the result than a Chiefs team that can still be 3-1 and in the hunt. ESPN FPI at 69.6 percent and Chiefs -4.5 on 47.5 is a favorite’s number on the road, not a bye. Polymarket at 8.6 percent to win the Super Bowl is the long-view tax on a 24-10 win that leaked first downs and nearly nine minutes.

What has to travel is the deep ball and the run-game spine, not the final score. Travis Kelce’s 48-yard catch down the middle set the opening touchdown; Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy each took 17-yard shots; Noah Gray gained 24; Rice took 34 down the sideline. That is the 2026 version of Mahomes that Arrowhead Pride says is back. Allegiant will dare Kansas City to finish those drives against Crosby and to keep Cousins from answering through the tight end. The next Sunday is the first real West measuring stick of the year.

lastGameReview.label: Week 3 · Sun, Sep 27 · 12:00 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: Kansas City beat Miami 24-10 at Hard Rock Stadium because the explosives and the takeaways outran a game Miami otherwise possessed. Two minutes and six seconds in, after Mahomes hit Kelce for 48 yards down the middle, J. Moore reported eligible and Walker went up the middle for a 10-yard touchdown and a 7-0 lead. Miami answered with a 3-yard touchdown at Q1 3:27 to tie it 7-7. Kansas City went back in front 14-7 on a 5-yard touchdown at Q2 12:58, then spent the rest of the afternoon protecting a lead while the Dolphins won first downs (19-18), third downs (8-16 to 3-7), rushing yards (119-88), and possession (34:21 to 25:39). A 37-yard Miami field goal at Q3 10:10 made it 14-10. Harrison Butker’s 34-yarder at Q4 11:35 pushed it to 17-10, and an 11-yard Kansas City touchdown at Q4 2:55 closed it 24-10.

analysis.body: The opening drive was the 2026 offense in miniature: a deep-middle answer to Kelce, then Walker finishing from 10 yards with Moore in the game. That is how you go 20-of-24 for 246 yards and still only post 18 first downs — you are living on chunk gainers, not on a chains-moving run game. Walker’s 18 carries for 70 yards and 20 touches were the volume; the other seven team rushes, including Emmett Johnson’s six carries and Mahomes’ one scramble, did not turn 88 rushing yards into a possession offense. When Kansas City needed a yard at the Miami 12, H. Nourzad reported eligible and Walker went up the middle for no gain, a turnover on downs at Q2 6:15.

Spagnuolo’s defense did not sack Willis (20-of-36, 61.1 rating, 0 sacks) and recorded 1 QB hit, but it did take the ball. At Q2 3:16, Willis went up the middle, L. Sneed forced the fumble, and Sneed recovered it. Nick Bolton led the tackle sheet with 11 and kept showing up in the run fits as Ollie Gordon took 17 rushes and 20 touches and Malik Willis added 9 rushes. De’Von Achane left early after an 11-yard run. The coverage tape was mixed: Greg Dulcich’s 42-yard catch down the middle in the third quarter was a seam shot Kansas City cannot give Kirk Cousins, and Miami still converted 8-of-16 on third down. The stop that mattered late was Karlaftis intercepting Willis short right at Q4 2:03, with Chris Jones on the play, after Kansas City had already gone up 24-10.

Mahomes was accurate without being asked to live in obvious passing downs all afternoon, and the 5 QB hits never became a sack. The miss was the deep-middle ball intended for Rice at Q2 2:00, intercepted by J. Rodriguez and returned 18 yards. Rice still led the receivers (7 for 88), Gray added the 24-yarder that set up Butker’s 34-yard field goal, and Thornton and Worthy each took a 17-yard shot. A Karlaftis illegal-use-of-hands penalty also wiped a C. Roland-Wallace interception on the last series. Efficient, not dominant. The scoreboard lied a little in Kansas City’s favor.

takeaways.title: Explosives covered a lost possession fight
takeaways.body: Mahomes at 20-of-24 for 246 yards and two touchdowns, plus Walker’s 10-yard opening score, produced 24 points on 18 first downs and 25:39 of possession. Miami’s 19 first downs, 8-of-16 on third down, and 34:21 with the ball are the numbers a 3-0 Raiders staff will put on the board first.

takeaways.title: Takeaways, not the pass rush, closed it
takeaways.body: Kansas City recorded 0 sacks and 1 QB hit. The defense still forced two Miami turnovers: Sneed’s forced-and-recovered fumble on Willis up the middle, and Karlaftis intercepting a short throw with Jones in the picture. That is how you win 24-10 while the opponent runs it 31 times.

takeaways.title: The deep ball showed up on schedule
takeaways.body: Kelce’s 48-yard catch, Thornton’s 17, Worthy’s 17, Gray’s 24, and Rice’s 34 are a real vertical day, not a dink tape. Third down at 3-of-7 is why those shots have to keep landing in Las Vegas, because the Chiefs are not yet staying on the field the hard way.

whatWorked: Mahomes 20-of-24, 246 yards, two touchdowns, 119.8 rating, 0 sacks allowed
Kelce’s 48-yard gain that set the opening score
L. Sneed force and recovery on the Willis fumble
Karlaftis interception of Willis at Q4 2:03
whatDidnt: 3-of-7 on third down and only 18 first downs
88 rushing yards on 25 carries as a team
0 sacks and 1 QB hit as a defense

currentState.lede: The Chiefs are 3-0 with a West road game that will not grade the Miami final score. They are a Mahomes-and-Walker team that can win 24-10 without winning downs or the clock, and that formula gets tested against Crosby, Cousins, and another unbeaten division roster on Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT.

workOn.title: Stay on the field on third down
workOn.body: A 3-of-7 afternoon in Miami is how you post 18 first downs and 25:39 of possession in a win. Allegiant will play the chains if Kansas City lives on explosives again. Mesh, Walker as an outlet, and the deep ball have to become a down-to-down menu, not a highlight reel.

workOn.title: Turn 88 rushing yards into a possession tape
workOn.body: Walker’s 70 yards on 18 carries traveled. The team’s 88 on 25 did not. If Crosby sets the edge and the Raiders sit on the cut, Bieniemy needs the boot and the screen as answers, not just another inside-zone call into a stacked box.

workOn.title: Get the pass rush on the glass
workOn.body: Chris Jones said the arrow is pointing up for Sack Nation after an 0-sack, 1-QB-hit tape against Willis. Cousins will not hold it forever if the interior is real, but Spagnuolo cannot bluff a rush that did not touch the quarterback last week. Simulated pressure has to be a call, not a hope.

workOn.title: Clean up the flags that give drives life
workOn.body: L. Sneed’s defensive holding, the offside, Humphrey’s illegal block, and Karlaftis’ illegal use of hands that wiped an interception are the opposite of a road-division formula. Mansoor Delane has already been fined for a low block in Miami. Allegiant will take the yards.

thinkAbout.title: Is 3-0 a style or a sample?
thinkAbout.body: Polymarket at 8.6 percent to win the Super Bowl and ESPN FPI at 69.6 percent for this game are not the same conversation. One is a road-favorite number against a 3-0 West club. The other is the market telling you a 24-10 win with 25:39 of possession is still probation.

thinkAbout.title: How much Walker is too much with Crosby across the line?
thinkAbout.body: Walker is the AFC Offensive Player of the Month and led the NFL in rushing yards through three weeks. He also just took 18 carries for 70 against a front that was not Maxx Crosby. The staff has to decide whether 20 touches is the identity or the tell.

thinkAbout.title: Who covers the Raiders tight ends?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict frames this as Kansas City’s toughest tight end test yet. Dulcich’s 42-yarder in Miami is the warning clip. Bolton, the safeties, and whatever Cole Christiansen is doing after the practice-squad elevation have to have a plan before Cousins starts the game in 12 personnel.

gamePlan.lede: Two 3-0 AFC West teams, Allegiant Stadium, CBS, Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT. Early control of the division is the assignment. Kansas City is the road favorite at -4.5 with ESPN FPI at 69.6 percent; the Raiders are the club that, as Arrowhead Addict put it, needs the win more. Treat it like a measuring stick, not a coronation.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Las Vegas counters with Crosby on the edge, Linderbaum’s interior leap, and Cousins playing above the replacement-level expectation. Spagnuolo has to rush a quarterback who will throw to tight ends and check the ball down if the first wave does not arrive. Kahlil Benson, Offensive Rookie of the Month and the starting left tackle through three games, is the protection hinge. The leverage is simple: if Kansas City runs into a box and sacks nobody, Cousins will keep the Raiders in a one-score game. If the Chiefs move Mahomes, stress the seams, and attack the interior, 3-0 vs. 3-0 becomes a West statement.

keys.title: Move the pocket away from Crosby
keys.body: Mahomes took 5 QB hits and 0 sacks in Miami. Crosby is a different rush. Boot, roll, and get Kelce and Rice on the moved-pocket throws so Benson is not asked to win every dropback on an island.

keys.title: Attack the interior, don’t just admire Linderbaum
keys.body: The Raiders’ line has taken a leap with Linderbaum, and Arrowhead Addict still says Kansas City can attack the interior. That is Jones, the stunts, and the simulated-pressure call — a way to stress Cousins, not a promise of a strip-sack.

keys.title: Take the tight end shot off the board
keys.body: Cover-2 and the hole player have to travel. Dulcich’s 42-yard catch is the clip Spagnuolo cannot replay against a Raiders 12-personnel menu. Two-deep, rally, and make Cousins throw the next one underneath to Bolton.

keys.title: Run Walker enough to keep four-minute math honest
keys.body: Eighteen carries and 70 yards is a spine, not a closing script. If Kansas City again sits on 88 team rushing yards and 25:39 of possession, Allegiant will play from ahead or from even and let Crosby hunt.

keys.title: Win third down without begging for explosives
keys.body: Mesh vs. man, Walker in the flat, and Rice as the rub winner are how you fix 3-of-7. The deep ball can still end a drive. It cannot be the only way you convert.

script: Open under-center with Walker on inside zone and make Las Vegas declare the box before Crosby can pin his ears back.
Hit four verticals early — Kelce or Gray on the seam, Rice or Worthy on the boundary — while the Raiders are still in a two-high look from the Miami tape.
Boot Mahomes away from Crosby on second-and-medium and throw the easy one to Kelce or the running back.
From 12 personnel, play Cover-2, take the TE shot, and let Bolton rally.
Call the zone blitz at the interior: show edge heat, drop a lineman, send a second-level rusher at Cousins’ first step.
If Crosby is flying upfield, throw the Walker screen and make the Raiders tackle in space.

nextGame.label: Week 4 · Sun, Oct 4 · 3:25 PM CT
nextGame.note: 3-0 vs. 3-0 in the AFC West; kickoff Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT, locally on KCTV-5.

spotlight.title: The deep ball is the live identity
spotlight.body: Kelce’s 48, Rice’s 34, Gray’s 24, Thornton’s 17, Worthy’s 17 — that is the tape Arrowhead Pride is pointing at when it says Mahomes’ deep ball is back. Allegiant will make him prove it against a pass rush that actually hunts.

spotlight.title: Walker has the month. The team still has 88.
spotlight.body: Kenneth Walker is AFC Offensive Player of the Month and led the NFL in rushing yards through three weeks. He also just went 18 for 70 with 20 touches in a game Kansas City ran for 88 as a team. Crosby is why that distinction matters.

spotlight.title: Benson’s month meets Crosby’s edge
spotlight.body: Kahlil Benson has started all three games at left tackle and is Offensive Rookie of the Month. Week 4 is not another tape against a backup rusher. Protection, chips, and boots have to be a plan, not a hope.

spotlight.title: Sack Nation is still waiting on a sack
spotlight.body: Jones says the arrow is pointing up. The Miami box says 0 sacks and 1 QB hit. Cousins and Linderbaum are the next test of whether that quote is a forecast or a wish.

spotlight.title: Christiansen is up; the TE test is real
spotlight.body: Kansas City elevated Cole Christiansen from the practice squad for this game after the Week 1 knee injury on the linebacker depth chart. Arrowhead Addict already framed the Raiders tight ends as the toughest test yet. That is not a coincidence.

spotlight.title: Las Vegas needs this one more
spotlight.body: Both clubs are 3-0, but the Raiders are the side with more riding on Sunday, and the Chiefs are the road favorite. A split here still leaves Kansas City in the hunt. A Raiders win rearranges the West before the Chargers even get a look in Week 6.

matchups.unit: Mahomes / deep ball vs. Raiders coverage
matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce
matchups.opponent: Las Vegas two-high and the deep-middle safety
matchups.note: The 48-yarder to Kelce and the 34-yarder to Rice are live answers. If Las Vegas sits in Cover-3, four verts is the call. If they play man, mesh is the call.

matchups.unit: Kahlil Benson / edge protection vs. Maxx Crosby
matchups.chiefs: Kahlil Benson, chips from the tight end, boots
matchups.note: Benson has started every game at left tackle and just won a rookie month. Crosby is still the best reason to move Mahomes instead of asking for 24 more dropbacks in a fixed pocket.

matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III (18 carries, 70 yards, 20 touches last game)
matchups.opponent: Las Vegas run fits with Crosby setting the edge
matchups.note: Walker can carry a game. Eighty-eight team rushing yards cannot. Inside zone has to win early or the boot and screen have to be ready.

matchups.unit: Spagnuolo pass rush vs. Cousins / Linderbaum
matchups.opponent: Kirk Cousins, Tyler Linderbaum, the improved interior
matchups.note: Miami got 0 sacks and 1 QB hit. The Raiders’ line has taken a leap, and the Chiefs can still attack the interior if they actually send it. Cousins will punish a rush that does not arrive.

matchups.unit: Chiefs second level vs. Raiders tight ends
matchups.opponent: Las Vegas 12 personnel and the TE seams
matchups.note: Dulcich’s 42-yard catch in Miami is the warning. This is the toughest tight end test on the calendar so far, and Cover-2 has to be more than a card in the meeting.

matchups.unit: Rice / Kelce vs. Raiders man coverage
matchups.chiefs: Rashee Rice (7 for 88), Travis Kelce (2 catches, including 48)
matchups.opponent: Raiders corners and the TE matcher
matchups.note: Rice is the volume winner. Kelce is the shot over the top. Mesh plus the seam is how Kansas City fixes 3-of-7 without asking Walker to convert every third-and-short.

xsandos.title: Walker inside zone, opening script
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, first two series at Allegiant, 21 or 12 personnel vs. the 3-0 Raiders
xsandos.why: Walker just took 18 carries for 70 and 20 touches; 88 team yards will not hold if Crosby sets the edge and the interior sits on the cut. Make Las Vegas tackle Walker before it can hunt Mahomes.
xsandos.coaching: Reid and Bieniemy: zone steps, one cut, Walker presses the line. Moore or the extra lineman only if you are in a reported-eligible look. Do not ask Benson to set the edge and pass-protect on the same series without a run fake first.

xsandos.title: Boot Mahomes away from Crosby
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 to 2nd-and-8 after a Walker run, Crosby aligned over Benson
xsandos.why: Five QB hits and 0 sacks in Miami is a pocket that got touched. Crosby is the next rusher. Sell Walker, move Mahomes, and throw the easy one to Kelce or the back before the edge can finish.
xsandos.coaching: Mahomes: sell the run, get outside, one-two read. Kelce leak or flat, Rice over the top, Walker check. Bieniemy, do not leave Benson on an island for a full drop when the fake is already bought.

xsandos.title: Four verts vs. their two-high
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-5 or a max-protect early-down shot vs. Las Vegas Cover-3 / two-high
xsandos.why: Kelce’s 48-yard catch and Rice’s 34-yarder are the 2026 deep ball. Stress the seams and the boundary before Cousins can answer. If the safety sits on Kelce, Worthy or Thornton runs past the corner.
xsandos.coaching: Kelce or Gray: stem the seam to the hash. Rice/Worthy: go. Mahomes: hitch and throw the window; do not hold it into Crosby. This is a called shot, not a scramble drill.

xsandos.title: Mesh to fix 3-of-7
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 to 3rd-and-7 vs. Raiders man, Rice and Kelce both in the route
xsandos.why: Kansas City went 3-of-7 on third down in Miami with 18 first downs. Rice’s 7 catches for 88 yards travel if you rub man; Kelce as the second crosser and Walker as the outlet keep Mahomes on schedule against Crosby’s rush.
xsandos.coaching: Rice and Kelce: tight mesh, don’t collide, win leverage. Thornton or Worthy: corner/sit. Walker: check down now, not later. Mahomes: take the first open crosser; the 48-yard shot is not the third-down answer every time.

xsandos.title: Cover-2 vs. Raiders 12 personnel
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-8, Las Vegas 12 personnel, Cousins looking at the tight end down the middle
xsandos.why: Dulcich’s 42-yard catch in Miami is the clip Cousins will copy. Two-deep takes the shot off the board; Bolton and the hole player rally. This is how you survive the toughest tight end test on the slate so far.
xsandos.coaching: Safeties: halves, no look-ins. Corners: hard corners, funnel. Bolton: fill the hole and tackle. Christiansen, if he is in, is a run-pass thumper, not a trail player on a seam. Make Cousins throw the next one underneath.

xsandos.title: Zone blitz at the interior
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-9 or 3rd-and-6 vs. Cousins, Linderbaum on the ball, need a hurry without selling out the seam
xsandos.why: The Raiders’ line has taken a leap, and the interior is still the place to stress Cousins. Show edge heat, drop a lineman, send a second-level rusher. This is a Spagnuolo call to use, not a claim that a blitz created a takeaway in Miami.
xsandos.coaching: Jones: stunt or drop on the call, don’t both rush the same gap. Second-level rusher: late, through the interior, eyes on Cousins’ first step. Behind it, play zone — the Miami 0-sack, 1-QB-hit tape does not get to repeat against a quarterback who will throw it if you leave a hole.

coaching.detail: The Miami protection held up in the sack column (0) and still allowed 5 QB hits. The adjustment is movement: boots, rollouts, and Walker as a threat so Benson is not the entire plan against Crosby.

Willis left with 20-of-36, 0 sacks, and two turnovers. Cousins will not give you the same scramble package, and he will find the tight end if the first wave is fake. Simulated pressure has to be real enough to change his feet.
Sack Nation’s CEO said the arrow is pointing up. The call sheet has to match the quote: interior games, a dropped lineman, a second-level rusher. Admiring Linderbaum is not a rush plan.
Three conversions in seven tries is why 24 points still felt like a stolen clock. Mesh, the checkdown, and one deep shot per series — not three deep shots and a punt.

personnel.move: Cole Christiansen elevated from the practice squad
personnel.detail: Kansas City made the linebacker eligible for the Raiders game after the Week 1 knee injury on the linebacker depth chart. He reverts after the game. With the Raiders tight ends on the menu, this is a coverage-and-run-fit add, not a ceremony.

personnel.move: Kahlil Benson, Offensive Rookie of the Month
personnel.detail: Benson has started all three games at left tackle. The next snap is Crosby. Chips, boots, and help have to be in the plan.

personnel.move: Kenneth Walker, AFC Offensive Player of the Month
personnel.detail: Walker led the NFL in rushing yards through three weeks and just took 18 carries for 70 with 20 touches in Miami. The staff still has to decide how much of the Allegiant script is him versus the boot-and-shot package.

personnel.move: Mansoor Delane fined for a low block
personnel.detail: The rookie corner was fined for unnecessary roughness in Miami. Technique has to clean up before a West road game gives Las Vegas free yards.

strategies: Script Walker inside zone until Las Vegas puts an eighth man in the box, then boot Mahomes the other way.
Take one deep shot in the first four plays — Kelce seam or Rice boundary — while the Raiders are still playing the Miami two-high tape.
Use Cover-2 as the base answer to 12 personnel and make Cousins throw underneath to Bolton.
Call zone blitz at the interior on a passing down; do not wait for Jones to win a one-on-one that Miami never gave him.
If Crosby is upfield, throw the Walker screen and let the line lead in space.
Keep Mahomes on third-down mesh instead of another deep-middle try like the Rodriguez interception.
Treat the kicking game as live: Butker missed from 50 in Miami, so the offense has to finish inside the 30.
debates: If Kansas City goes 3-1, is this still a Super Bowl roster, or did Allegiant just expose the Miami clock?
How many of Walker’s 20 touches should survive a Crosby game?
Is Sack Nation a Week 4 problem or a three-week trend?
Do you trust Benson one-on-one, or do you chip Crosby even if it costs you a Kelce route?
Are the Raiders tight ends a schematic issue or a personnel issue for this second level?
Does ESPN FPI at 69.6 percent have this right, or is -4.5 a trap number against another 3-0 West club?

runOfShow.talkTrack: 24-10 in Miami, Mahomes 20-of-24 for 246, and the Dolphins still had the ball 34:21. That is the open. Then: two 3-0 West teams, Allegiant, Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT, Crosby next.

Walk through the Walker 10-yard score 2:06 in after Kelce’s 48, the 14-7 lead, Sneed’s fumble, the Rodriguez interception, Butker’s 34-yarder, the 11-yard touchdown to make it 24-10, and Karlaftis taking the Willis throw. Hit 88 rush, 3-of-7, 18 first downs, 0 sacks, 5 QB hits on Mahomes, 1 KC QB hit.

Separate the scoreboard from the tape. Work-ons: third down, the run-game total, the pass rush, the flags. Walker’s month vs. the team’s 88. Jones saying the arrow is up. Polymarket 8.6 percent vs. FPI 69.6 percent.
Give Las Vegas credit: 3-0, Cousins above expectation, Linderbaum, Crosby, tight ends. How they match. Benson. Christiansen. Cover-2 and the interior pressure call. Keys and the script.
Four offense cards — inside zone, boot, four verts, mesh — then Cover-2 and the zone blitz as calls for this game. Tie each one to Walker, Crosby, Rice, Kelce, Cousins, Jones.
Hit the fan arguments: Super Bowl roster vs. the Miami clock, how much Walker, whether -4.5 is a trap. Close on Week 4 as West control, not a bye. Remind: CBS, Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT.
